name: M2 Centralized Exchange
classificationNote: Classified by TypeSafe jev-1.13.0 (confidence 0.95). Replaced keyword guess "key-compromise".
rootCause: On October 31, 2024, Abu Dhabi-based centralized exchange M2 suffered a breach of its hot wallets on Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana, resulting in the theft of approximately $13.7 million in digital assets. The attacker exploited an access-control weakness in the exchange's hot wallet infrastructure, enabling unauthorized asset transfers. M2 quickly detected the incident and reportedly reimbursed affected users, but has not released detailed technical disclosures or a post-mortem. An access-control vulnerability in M2's hot wallet infrastructure enabled unauthorized transactions, allowing an attacker to bypass wallet authorization and extract assets across several chains.
